# Soundboard

A free (GPL-3), offline Android app for mixing looping ambient sounds: pick
audio files from your device, play any number of them at once, and set each
one's volume independently. Kotlin + Jetpack Compose + Media3, single Gradle
module, no backend.

## Start Here

- `README.md`: overview, tooling, quickstart.
- `SPEC.md`: the MVP product spec (deleted once the MVP ships).
- `AGENTS.md`: agent operating instructions, including the audio rules.
- `DECISIONS.md`: this project's architecture decisions and why.
- `docs/tooling.md`: pinned dependency versions.
- `docs/development.md`: local development runbook and manual audio checks.

## Key Conventions

- No network calls, no `INTERNET` permission, no telemetry — everything is local.
- Audio files are referenced by persisted SAF URI and never copied into the app.
- One ExoPlayer per sound; audio focus is held once, centrally, for the app.
- The engine lives in the `Application`; the foreground service only keeps the
  process alive and shows the notification.
- No dependency injection framework; one hand-rolled composition root.
- Dependencies must be free software (F-Droid requirement) — see `DECISIONS.md`.

## Validation

```bash
./gradlew check
```

Unit tests cover pure logic only. Playback, mixing, and the foreground service
need a real device.
